goals: Provide a deterministic, learnable sculk-vibration outcome when players intentionally prepare ordinary chests with a mostly sealed, wool-lined enclosure.
Remain a standalone Fabric utility without Matcha coupling for Ancient City use and other worlds.
scope: Target only minecraft:chest container open and close game events at the actual emitting chest position.
Evaluate exactly north, south, east, west, and down; suppress the event only when at least four faces are sealed by full collision blocks and at least two of those full blocks are in minecraft:wool.
Evaluate double-chest component emissions independently, so complete silence requires both halves to satisfy the same rule.

exclusions: The top face is intentionally never evaluated.
Trapped chests, barrels, ender chests, shulker boxes, and every unrelated container remain outside block coverage.
Global wool occlusion, general vibration propagation, and any new sculk behavior remain unchanged.
Chest sound, lid animation, opener counts, inventory behavior, and unrelated walking, placement, breaking, projectile, eating, and mob vibrations remain vanilla.
This migration does not deploy to Minecraft, mutate either test slot or the accepted physical Workbench, or change Test Instance Manager state.

dependencies.reason: Exact game version whose ContainerOpenersCounter call sites and chest behavior are targeted.
Required loader declared by the retained standalone artifact; Fabric API is not required.
Compilation and runtime baseline declared by the retained implementation.

state.milestone: C1 passed the focused runtime scope and is accepted for the intended vanilla Ancient City behavior.
